status: Exploratory pilot settings fixed before this model fit; NOT prospective registration or independent testing
study_question: Can a compact image model rank blood-annotated frames within the existing sparse Galar sample more effectively than an untrained red-excess score and outcome-blind sampling?
data: Verified Galar v2 corrected annotations and existing 512-image-per-examination sample; no additional frames accessed
task: binary explicit blood label; not active bleeding or all-pathology detection
model: same capsule-cnn-v1 architecture with two outputs, no pretrained weights, inverse-frequency training-class weights, CPU

training_budget.best_checkpoint: lowest unweighted historical development cross entropy

metrics: binary AUROC where both labels exist
positive frame recall at 5, 10 and 25 percent per-examination sampling budget
per-examination results and false positive review selections
important_prior_evidence: Prior public results and training-only audit already revealed exam 7 dominates training blood positives, exam 9 has no blood positives, and exam 10 has positives. No claim of blind model selection.
limits: no lesion/interval sensitivity or clinical reading-time evidence
